reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator promotes staking USDC through Bybit with a claim of earning 13,000 per day and demonstrates a calculation presenting an extremely large daily return. The creator directs viewers to enroll and stake, while the video shows a 500% APR offer and then a separate BTC multiplication site, presenting speculative or extraordinary gains as an actionable earning opportunity rather than reporting or testing a third-party scam. The visible Bybit purchase eligibility requirements provide some context, but do not qualify the video's daily-earnings pitch.

citations.quote: Stake USDC, Earn 13k Per Day | Enroll now

opening.argument: Judge the earnings language alongside the limits the presentation actually shows. The USDC offer is restricted to users meeting identity-verification and deposit conditions, and the screen caps participation at 300 USDC per user. That is materially different from an unrestricted promise that anyone can collect the headline amount. The accompanying description also includes a Ponzi warning. These details do not prove the offer is sound, but they support reading the video as discussion of a conditional promotion, not a guaranteed payout to every viewer.

citations.quote: Stake USDC, Earn 13k Per Day | Enroll now

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title and spoken daily figure are forceful, but they do not erase the on-screen eligibility failure and per-user cap. Nor does a calculator result establish that the displayed number is an available daily withdrawal. The separate BTC page does not, by itself, establish that the USDC offer pays that result.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cap and eligibility conditions qualify access to the offer; they do not qualify the creator's headline invitation to stake USDC and earn 13k per day. The description's brief warning names a different scheme and does not warn that this earnings pitch is unreliable. The 500% offer and large-return calculation reinforce the pitch rather than neutralize it.

citations.quote: Stake USDC, Earn 13k Per Day | Enroll now

opening.argument: Much of the presentation walks through how the displayed promotions work: a dated event lists registration, deposit and trade tasks, while a later screen shows the USDC offer refusing a purchase because its requirements have not been met. The calculator shows an arithmetic operation; it does not show funds arriving in an account. The speaker also says viewers will be given a step-by-step guide. Taken together, these are features of an operational walkthrough, even if its title uses an aggressive earnings hook.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats the calculator and the separate BTC activity as proof of one actionable earnings path. The calculator demonstrates a computation, not a payment; the BTC screen shows a timed free-play page, not a USDC staking return. The purchase-failure screen is omitted from that reading despite showing that participation is conditional.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can still promote an earning opportunity. Here the title explicitly pairs staking USDC with 13k per day and tells viewers to enroll. The speaker repeats the daily figure while discussing staking, and the calculator supplies a large numerical result from a 500% input. Showing requirements does not turn that promotional framing into neutral instruction.

opening.argument: The observable transaction is a set of ordinary promotional offers and referral links, not evidence that this creator controls a pool or receives viewers' deposits. The event materials specify tasks and prize eligibility; the description lists multiple exchange rewards and invitations; and the USDC screen presents an offer inside a savings interface with an eligibility check. None of those cited materials shows a request to send funds or credentials directly to the creator. The earnings headline deserves scrutiny, but promotional language alone does not establish that the creator runs a fraudulent investment scheme.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The concern is the promoted staking-return claim, not proof that the creator personally collects deposits. The title urges viewers to stake USDC for 13k per day; the USDC offer displays 500% APR; and the calculator applies 500% to a large principal. Referral links and eligibility rules do not make that earnings presentation ordinary rewards content.
